evidence.claim: Amnesty said Russia had blocked independent media, banned Facebook and Twitter, and arbitrarily arrested more than 13,800 people at anti-war rallies since 24 February 2022.
evidence.title: Russia: Kremlin’s ruthless crackdown stifles independent journalism and anti-war movement
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Russia had blocked independent media, banned Facebook and Twitter, and arbitrarily arrested more than 13,800 people at anti-war rallies since 24 February 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 field summary with an explicit arrest count and named restrictions.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the first two weeks of the full-scale war and its domestic repression response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The crackdown was carried out by Russian authorities under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The arrest figure is a monitoring estimate, not an official government total.

evidence.claim: HRW said Putin signed laws on 4 March 2022 that criminalized independent war reporting and anti-war protest, with penalties of up to 15 years in prison.
evidence.title: Russia Criminalizes Independent War Reporting, Anti-War Protests
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Putin signed laws on 4 March 2022 that criminalized independent war reporting and anti-war protest, with penalties of up to 15 years in prison.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific law-adoption dates and penalties are named in a contemporaneous HRW report.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 domestic repression wave.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The laws were signed by Putin and enforced by his state institutions.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the laws as anti-disinformation measures.

evidence.claim: Reuters reporting republished by Euronews said police detained more than 4,300 people at anti-war protests across Russia and that one protester was shown beaten on the ground by riot police.
evidence.title: More than 4,300 detained at anti-war protests in Russia
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reporting republished by Euronews said police detained more than 4,300 people at anti-war protests across Russia and that one protester was shown beaten on the ground by riot police.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters-reported protest tally with concrete police-violence detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The detentions were carried out by Russian police under Putin's government.
contrary_evidence: Reuters noted it could not independently verify some social-media footage.

evidence.claim: Freedom House reported that Russia blocked more than 5,000 websites after the invasion, expanded state blocking powers, and deepened self-censorship around war, corruption, and LGBT topics.
evidence.title: Russia: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House reported that Russia blocked more than 5,000 websites after the invasion, expanded state blocking powers, and deepened self-censorship around war, corruption, and LGBT topics.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed country report with explicit 2022 findings and explanatory text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These were state actions under Putin's rule, primarily through Roskomnadzor and allied agencies.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes broad internet access remained widespread, so the issue is control and censorship rather than total shutdown.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the Russian authorities used severe reprisals, arbitrary arrests, force, detentions, and heavy fines to crush public protest and suppress reporting by journalists and monitors.
evidence.title: Russian journalists are being silenced to stifle reporting of protests
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the Russian authorities used severe reprisals, arbitrary arrests, force, detentions, and heavy fines to crush public protest and suppress reporting by journalists and monitors.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Focused 2022 report with clear domestic-safety implications and detailed methods of repression.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The suppression is attributable to Russian state authorities under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes the anti-war movement still generated protests despite the crackdown.

evidence.claim: Memorial said political prisoners in Russia reached 513 by the end of 2022 and described the year as a turning point for harsher repression.
evidence.title: We publish a report on political prisoners and political repression in Russia in 2022
evidence.excerpt: Memorial said political prisoners in Russia reached 513 by the end of 2022 and described the year as a turning point for harsher repression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialized political-prisoner monitoring project summarizing its 2022 annual report with explicit counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The political repression occurred under Putin's state system.
contrary_evidence: The figure is an incomplete list and therefore a conservative count.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that torture and ill-treatment by law-enforcement officials persisted in 2022, including beatings, electroshock, waterboarding allegations, and punishment cells for Navalny and Yuri Dmitriyev.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that torture and ill-treatment by law-enforcement officials persisted in 2022, including beatings, electroshock, waterboarding allegations, and punishment cells for Navalny and Yuri Dmitriyev.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual report with specific 2022 incidents, official in time for 2022 conduct assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Covers March to October 2022 domestic policing and prison abuse.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These abuses occurred under Putin's security and prison system.
contrary_evidence: The report describes specific incidents and allegations; it does not claim all custody abuse was centrally directed in each case.

evidence.claim: HRW said the State Duma backed legislation that would further restrict LGBT expression, including positive or neutral information about LGBT people, with hefty fines and broader stigmatization.
evidence.title: Russia: Expanded 'Gay Propaganda' Ban Progresses Toward Law
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the State Duma backed legislation that would further restrict LGBT expression, including positive or neutral information about LGBT people, with hefty fines and broader stigmatization.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear late-2022 legislative analysis with legal and rights implications spelled out.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 domestic vulnerability and incitement environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This legislative trajectory occurred under Putin and his ruling coalition.
contrary_evidence: Lawmakers said they were defending morality and 'traditional values'.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Russia expanded its LGBT-propaganda ban to all ages, with fines and possible arrest for foreigners, in a move critics said was meant to intimidate and oppress sexual minorities.
evidence.title: Russia's parliament passes law banning 'LGBT propaganda' among adults
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Russia expanded its LGBT-propaganda ban to all ages, with fines and possible arrest for foreigners, in a move critics said was meant to intimidate and oppress sexual minorities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-reported legislative coverage with direct details on scope and penalties.
evidence.period_fit: Exactly within 2022 and directly relevant to vulnerable-group protection.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The law was being pushed and would be signed under Putin's authority.
contrary_evidence: The government framed it as a morality and child-protection measure.

evidence.claim: Meduza reported that Putin publicly denounced a 'fifth column' of 'traitors' and praised 'purification of society,' while claiming Russia was forced into war and that troops were avoiding civilian casualties.
evidence.title: ‘The purification of society will only strengthen the country’ Meduza’s brief retelling of Putin’s darkest speech yet
evidence.excerpt: Meduza reported that Putin publicly denounced a 'fifth column' of 'traitors' and praised 'purification of society,' while claiming Russia was forced into war and that troops were avoiding civilian casualties.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Directly reports a specific Putin speech with language relevant to incitement and fear climate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The rhetoric is directly attributable to Putin.
contrary_evidence: The article is a retelling rather than a Kremlin transcript.

evidence.claim: OVD-Info describes Russia as a place where politically motivated detentions, interrogations, searches, and arrests occur regularly and says it collects and publishes repression data for the public.
evidence.title: ОВД-Инфо
evidence.excerpt: OVD-Info describes Russia as a place where politically motivated detentions, interrogations, searches, and arrests occur regularly and says it collects and publishes repression data for the public.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Current project homepage describing mission and scale, useful for mapping the domestic repression information environment but not a year-specific report.
evidence.period_fit: General repression-context source rather than a 2022 incident report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The project describes repression under the Russian state system led by Putin.
contrary_evidence: This is a live organizational homepage, so it is weaker than a dated annual report for year-specific claims.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said at least 1,386 peaceful protesters were detained across Russia after Putin's partial mobilization call, and police used unnecessary and excessive force including beatings and chokeholds; some detainees also faced summons to enlistment centres.
evidence.title: Russia: More than 1,300 protesters detained after Putin's partial military draft
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said at least 1,386 peaceful protesters were detained across Russia after Putin's partial mobilization call, and police used unnecessary and excessive force including beatings and chokeholds; some detainees also faced summons to enlistment centres.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous human-rights reporting with a concrete detention count and detailed policing description; strong for the repression mechanism, though based on Amnesty and OVD-Info reporting rather than direct state admission.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the crackdown followed Putin's mobilization call and was enforced by state police under his government.
contrary_evidence: Russian authorities treated anti-mobilization protests as unlawful and framed mobilization as necessary for the war effort.

evidence.claim: Committee experts said there had been thousands of cases of harassment and persecution of journalists, dozens of murders and attempted murders, journalists abducted and tortured, hundreds of Russian journalists detained for reporting on the war or protests, and mass arrests in response to peaceful demonstrations.
evidence.title: Human Rights Committee Considers Report of the Russian Federation in the Absence of a Delegation, Experts Raise Issues on the Persecution of Journalists and the Arrests of Protesters
evidence.excerpt: Committee experts said there had been thousands of cases of harassment and persecution of journalists, dozens of murders and attempted murders, journalists abducted and tortured, hundreds of Russian journalists detained for reporting on the war or protests, and mass arrests in response to peaceful demonstrations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN meeting summary of treaty-body review with direct expert statements and concrete allegations; strong independent corroboration of repression patterns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the discussion concerned conduct by Russian authorities and Russian forces during Putin's 2022 rule.
contrary_evidence: Russian officials and aligned media disputed the scale and legitimacy of the allegations.

evidence.claim: Committee experts said reports since February 2022 included excessive force, extrajudicial executions, torture, rape and sexual violence, forced conscription of civilians, and in September 2022 the detention and beating of 20 women who protested the conscription of Chechens; they also described serious and continuous violations and widespread impunity in Chechnya and anti-LGBT violence in the North Caucasus.
evidence.title: Human Rights Committee Considers Report of the Russian Federation in the Absence of a Delegation, Experts Raise Issues on the Persecution of Journalists and the Arrests of Protesters
evidence.excerpt: Committee experts said reports since February 2022 included excessive force, extrajudicial executions, torture, rape and sexual violence, forced conscription of civilians, and in September 2022 the detention and beating of 20 women who protested the conscription of Chechens; they also described serious and continuous violations and widespread impunity in Chechnya and anti-LGBT violence in the North Caucasus.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN expert summary with specific examples, victim groups, and attribution to Russian-controlled or tolerated conduct; strong for domestic safety and vulnerable-group abuse.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the conduct was described as occurring under Russian state or tolerated regional authority within Putin's federal system, including conscription enforcement and Chechnya-related abuses.
contrary_evidence: Russian authorities denied or minimized such allegations and presented the cases as lawful security or morality enforcement.
